deep.reconstruction:
The page is a scratch computation, most of it struck through by a large X. The problem is classical. Take a small category A, its presheaf topos A^ (written C' = A^), a cocomplete category with universal colimits 𝒳 (written C = 𝒳, presumably a topos), and a functor φ: A → 𝒳. One gets the usual adjoint pair:
- u = φ^*: 𝒳 → A^, given by u(F) = (α ↦ Hom(φ(α), F)). This is the 'nerve' or restriction functor, and it is continuous.
- v = φ_!: A^ → 𝒳, given by v(G) = colim_{x ∈ A/G} φ(x). This is the left Kan extension or 'realization' functor, and it is cocontinuous.
This is the SGA4 I formalism; the words 'continu / cocontinu' match SGA4 usage.

The question being tested is when φ_! commutes with finite products. Every presheaf is a colimit of representables: F = colim_{A/F} α and G = colim_{A/G} β. Colimits in A^ are universal, so F×G = colim_{A/F} (α×G) = colim_{A/F} colim_{A/G} (α×β) = colim_{A/F × A/G} (α×β). Since φ_! is cocontinuous, φ_!(F×G) = colim_{A/F×A/G} φ_!(α×β). The boxed key condition is φ_!(α×β) ≅ φ_!(α)×φ_!(β) = φ(α)×φ(β) for representables α, β. Granting it, and using universality of colimits in 𝒳, one gets φ_!(F×G) ≅ φ_!(F)×φ_!(G). So φ_! preserves binary products as soon as it does so on pairs of representables.

The bottom lines (𝒳 → A^, Y ↦ (a_i ↦ φ^*(Y)), φ(a_i) → Y) restate the nerve functor through maps φ(a_i) → Y.

The top sketch shows E_n = [1,n] split as E_p ⊔ E'_q, the shifted copy via β_{n,q}, with a point α and E∖{α}. This ties to the previous page's maps α_{n,p}, β_{n,q} and the surjectivity condition (**) E_{p+q}^* → E_p^* × E_q^*. The context is presumably a combinatorial category A built from the sets [1,n] (with symmetric groups, inclusions ∂_n and retractions k_n), whose 'realizations' in Ens or a topos should be product-compatible. The aim is likely a description of the stratified-topos combinatorics of 'Topos stratifié', though the page alone does not show this.
errors: No real error. The product α×β of two representables is generally not representable in A^, so φ_!(α×β) is not simply φ(α×β). The boxed isomorphism φ_!(α×β) ≅ φ(α)×φ(β) is a hypothesis to be checked, not automatic. It would hold if A has finite products preserved by φ.
One must also have universal colimits (products commuting with colimits in each variable) in 𝒳 for the last step. This holds when 𝒳 is a topos.
Using the product of comma categories A/F × A/G as the indexing category is legitimate because the colimits are taken separately in each variable.

ideas.what: Adjunction φ_! ⊣ φ^* between presheaves on A and a cocomplete category 𝒳, induced by φ: A → 𝒳 (nerve/realization)
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exposé I (and IV), also Pursuing Stacks

ideas.what: Criterion: φ_! preserves finite products if it preserves products of pairs of representables, using density of representables and universality of colimits
ideas.modern_name: Product-preserving left Kan extensions (e.g. geometric realization preserves products; Day convolution/Segal-type arguments)
